messages.content: "你能告訴我著名足球運動員莱萊納爾·梅西的淨資產是多少歐元嗎？之後，我想知道籃球運動員勒布朗·詹姆斯的淨資產是多少英鎊。此外，我對一個使用公制系統的重85公斤、身高180公分的人的身體質量指數（BMI）也很好奇。最後，你能計算一個使用英制系統的重200磅、身高6英呎2英吋的人的BMI嗎？"

function.name: calculate_bmi
function.description: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

weight.description: Weight of the person in kilograms.

height.description: Height of the person in centimeters.

unit.description: Optional parameter to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems. Default is 'metric'.

function.name: celebrity_net_worth_get
function.description: Get the total net worth of a sports celebrity based on most recent data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the sports celebrity.

currency.description: The currency in which the net worth will be returned. Default is 'USD'.

2. Net worth of LeBron James in pounds sterling (£).

3. BMI calculation for metric system: weight=85 kg, height=180 cm.

4. BMI calculation for imperial system: weight=200 lbs, height=6 ft 2 inches.

But we need to call each with appropriate parameters.

For Messi's net worth: name="Lionel Messi", currency="EUR".

For LeBron: name="LeBron James", currency="GBP". But note "currency" param expects string; maybe use "£"? It says default USD but can specify other currencies like EUR or GBP? We'll pass "EUR" and "GBP".

Then BMI calculations: For metric: weight=85, height=180, unit='metric'.

Imperial: weight=200, height=?? We need convert feet+inches into something. The function signature has weight in kilograms and height in centimeters if using metric. If using imperial, likely weight in pounds and height in inches? Actually description: "Optional parameter to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems." So we set unit='imperial', weight=200, height=? Should provide height in inches? They gave height as 6ft 2in -> that's 74 inches. So height=74. Provide unit='imperial'.

Thus we make four separate calls.

We'll do them sequentially. Use assistant->commentary to call functions. Then respond with results.
